blocks.content: I found the spot by accident, the way I always do.

The corner of Bellamy and March, where the old hardware store used to be. The building's been empty for three years and someone has started leaving flower pots on the front steps — different ones every few weeks, like they're quietly making a case for the place. Today there were two terracotta pots with something purple in them that caught the morning light at exactly the angle I'd been looking for.
I was setting my bag down, considering whether this was actually the spot or whether I was just settling, when I heard the laugh.
Same one as the bus stop. The kind that didn't ask permission before it happened.
I looked up before I'd made a conscious decision to.

She was across the street with another girl — dark curls, talking fast, the way two people talk when they've been having the same conversation for years and know they can skip the setup. The dinosaur was still under her arm. Tucked like she'd never once thought about putting it down, which she probably hadn't.
She was pointing at something down the street. Making a case for it. The other girl was not convinced. This, somehow, made her make the case harder.
I'm aware that I was staring.
She glanced back over her shoulder — mid-story, turning to gesture at something behind them — and for half a second she was looking directly at the corner where I was standing.
She didn't see me. Or she saw the general area. The way you look when you're looking at a story, not a person.
Then they turned the corner and she was gone.
I stood at the corner of Bellamy and March for longer than I want to admit, holding my bag and my coffee, looking at an empty street.
The flower pots were still nice.
